title: Your own film character for a frame
description: Adjust color and grain, save the combination of settings and check the result on export.

blocks.text: A photographer wants to repeat his own combination of color and grain. A ready-made filter name is little help if it is not clear what exactly it changes and how to fix the result under different light.

quote.text: Very cool and unique in that you basically build custom film presets from the ground up. You can make your own film that may not even exist. However, I really wish the filters didn’t have original names.

blocks.text: Carrying the edit through to a result

The settings can be assembled and saved under a name of your own. Applied to another frame, the overall color base stays while exposure and local areas are edited separately. Before export, the final dimensions are visible.
Where the idea has an advantage

The first set is worth testing on different source files and with the chosen way of showing them. The word “film” on its own gives no advantage. The usefulness is in a controllable repeat of the author’s decision, not in a promise of an exact copy of any film stock.
